title: Why Do Bananas Ripen Faster Next to Apples?
short_title: Why Fruit Rots Faster Next to Apples (A Hidden Gas!)
description: Fruit gives off an invisible gas called ethylene that tells nearby fruit to ripen. Here is the simple science, and how to make your fruit last longer.
comment: Where do you keep your bananas? Tell me below!

scenes.text: Why do bananas turn brown so fast when they sit next to apples? The fruits are talking to each other.
Many fruits give off an invisible gas called ethylene. It is a ripening signal.
Apples make a lot of it. When the gas reaches a banana, the banana switches on its ripening program, and it softens, sweetens, and turns yellow, then brown.
A closed bag traps the gas, so fruit ripens even faster. That is great for a hard avocado, but bad for fruit you want to keep.
To make fruit last, keep apples away from other fruit, and let the air move.
